code-summary="Show the code"} library(ggplot2) library(tidyverse) z_values <- seq(-3, 3, by = 0.01) probabilities <- dnorm(z_values) df <- data.frame(Z = z_values, probability = probabilities) arrows <- tibble( x1 = c(2.2), x2 = c(3.3), y1 = c(.02), y2 = c(0.15) ) p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Z, y = probability)) + geom_line( size = 1.2, color = "#e8601d" ) + geom_ribbon( data = subset(df, Z >= 1.96), aes(ymax = probability, ymin = 0), fill = "goldenrod", alpha = 0.5) + geom_vline( xintercept = 1.96, linetype = "dashed", color = "black" ) + geom_text( x = 0.6, y = 0.04, label = alpha = 0.1, label.size = 0, size = 5, parse = TRUE, hjust = -0.2) + labs( x = expression(italic(Z)), y = "probability density", ) + geom_curve( data = arrows, aes(x = x1, y = y1, xend = x2, yend = y2), arrow = arrow( length = unit(0.1, "inch"), angle = 30), size = 1, color = "gray30", curvature = 0.4 ) p #library(plotly) #ggplotly(p) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Standard normal distribution Dat bestand moet bovenaan ieder document worden ingeladen (zie eerste regel van dit bestand). ### Voorbeelden: Voor kansverdelingen heb ik de macro \\pr{} gedefineerd: $$\pr{A \cap B} = \pr{A} \pr{B | A}.$$ $$\pr{A \cup B} = \pr{A} + \pr{B} - \pr{A \cap B}.$$ Voor de verwachtingswaarde de macro \\ev{}: $$\ev{X} = \sum_x x\, \pr{X = x}.$$ De differentiaaloperator is \\diff: $$ \ev{X} = \int_{-\infty}^\infty x\, \pr{X = x} \diff x. $$ Voor varianties \\var{}: $$ \var{X} = \sum_x \left(x - \ev{X}\right)^2 \, \pr{X = x} $$ $$ \var{X} = \int_{-\infty}^\infty \left(x - \ev{X}\right)^2 \, \pr{X = x} \diff x. $$ Voor standaarddeviaties \\sd{}: $$ \sd{X} = \sqrt{\var{X}}. $$ ### Mermaid Met Mermaid kun je heel gemakkelijk diagrammen maken: ```{mermaid} %%| label: fig-variables %%| caption: "Typen variabelen" flowchart TB A(Variabelen) --> C("Categoriaal (Kwalitatief)") A --> B("Numeriek (Kwantitatief)") B --> F(Discreet) B --> G(Continu) C --> E(Nominaal) C --> D(Ordinaal) ``` ### Callouts We kunnen gebruik maken van call-outs: ::: callout-note Note that there are five types of callouts, including: `note`, `warning`, `important`, `tip`, and `caution`. ::: ::: callout-tip ## Tip with Title This is an example of a callout with a title. ::: ::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"} ## Expand To Learn About Collapse This is an example of a 'folded' caution callout that can be expanded by the user.
